hero.heading: MSP Manufacturing, a cost model sent for correction
hero.caption: Built September 26, 2026, from Purdue MEP and NIST success stories, the Conexus Indiana case study, company pages, and federal data. Every number is labeled: published, federal, or our assumption. The assumptions are sliders; move them and the number moves.
hero.liveCaption: The model's estimate, on the assumptions you have set below
hero.subline: Exact computed endpoints: $9,162.50 and $90,540.00, rounded to the nearest $5,000 for display.

model.heading: Move our assumptions
model.intro: Each slider is one of the assumptions in our letter, set to the range we wrote down. If you know a figure, narrow its range, or close both handles on the exact number. The estimate above then follows your figures instead of ours. Tap a figure to type it exactly.

volume.label: Jobs you release in a year
volume.caption: Optional. Type your volume and every dollar figure on this page scales to your year. Leave it empty and the model stays per hundred jobs.

sliders.label: Jobs reworked or re-run, by any cause
Average value of a released job
Months a fixed quote waits between signature and delivery

presets.label: We buy materials the day we quote

constants.text: Aluminum mill shapes rose 25.3 percent from September 2025 to August 2026 [[BENCHMARK]], BLS series WPU102501. This one is not a slider.

terms.label: Rework and re-runs at job value

model.formulaText: Leak per 100 jobs = 100 × rework rate × job value + 100 × job value × materials share × 0.253 × (months / 12)
model.plainText: In words, the jobs that get reworked or re-run at their released value, plus the slice of this year's aluminum rise a fixed quote absorbs while it waits between signature and delivery.
model.callout: You publish your certifications; they prove your parts conform. Nobody certifies the hours a job waits between operations against the hours it spends being cut, or what a held quote absorbed while aluminum moved. Those numbers exist in your records, unread.

respect.heading: What you already show in the open
paragraphs: Your parts fly on virtually every major commercial and military aircraft [[OBSERVED]].
You carry six certifications: NADCAP, AS9100, ISO 9001, ITAR, Boeing, FAA [[OBSERVED]].
Your business grew thirty percent in a year, in a federal success story [[BENCHMARK]].
Your family bought this shop in 2002; it has made parts since 1943 [[BENCHMARK]].
Your president sits on Purdue MEP's board of advisors [[BENCHMARK]].
